## Prebuilt binaries

`ucal` for Linux, macOS and Windows. Unpack and run — there is nothing to
install and no runtime to provide.

| file | for |
|---|---|
| `*-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | Linux, Intel/AMD — statically linked, any distribution |
| `*-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | Linux, ARM64 |
| `*-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | macOS, Intel |
| `*-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` | macOS, Apple silicon |
| `*-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` | Windows |

Each was built from this tag and had to reproduce the project's declared
constants — `ucal verify`, which exits non-zero if it cannot — before it was
packaged.

**With one exception, named rather than glossed:** the Intel macOS build is
cross-compiled from an Apple-silicon runner, which cannot execute it, so that
one artefact was not self-checked. Run `ucal verify` yourself after unpacking;
it takes no arguments and no network.

**`SHA256SUMS.txt` is not signed, and is weaker evidence than it looks.** It was
generated by the same CI job that produced the files, so it shows a download
arrived intact and nothing more. The one artefact this project actually signs is
`fixtures/SHA256SUMS.minisig`, over the conformance vectors, with a key held on
one laptop — `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` says what that does and does not establish.

Reproducibility is not claimed: nothing pins the compiler version. To check a
binary rather than trust it, build it from this tag.

macOS refuses to run an unsigned download until the quarantine attribute is
cleared: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./ucal`.

New here? `ucal datum` states what tick 0 is and what is not being claimed about
it; `ucal verify` prints the constants and says plainly that agreeing with
itself is not verification. `CLI.md` is in the archive.
